title: Nonreentrant proximal fascicular ventricular tachycardia, with normal QRS duration and normal axis, originating from a region remote from the His bundle
case_prompt: A 48-year-old woman was referred with uncontrolled tachycardia. One year earlier, she had received an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator for complete atrioventricular block and ventricular fibrillation arrest. Echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and blood tests showed no structural abnormalities; positron-emission tomography was unremarkable. An endomyocardial biopsy was not performed. After device implantation, a tachycardia initiated and terminated incessantly with atrioventricular dissociation. The R-R interval was completely irregular (cycle length 384–560 ms, mean 441 ms). The QRS duration during tachycardia was 74 ms, with a normal axis and no bundle-branch-block pattern. Bisoprolol, verapamil, and bepridil failed to suppress the tachycardia. Multipolar electrode catheters were placed in the high right atrium, His-bundle region, and right ventricular apex. At baseline, there was complete A-H block during sinus rhythm and no His potential identified. Ventriculoatrial conduction was absent during ventricular pacing. During tachycardia, the His-bundle catheter recorded His potentials preceding QRS onset by 34 ms. The tachycardia could not be entrained, and ventricular pacing produced a QRS morphology dissimilar to the tachycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation was performed under guidance of an electroanatomical mapping system.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Supraventricular tachycardia (AVNRT, orthodromic reentrant tachycardia with nodoventricular/nodofascicular pathways) was considered but excluded — “supraventricular tachycardia was less likely because of the complete AV block … These diagnoses can be excluded by their demonstrating longer HV intervals during sinus rhythm than during tachycardia.”  
2. Junctional ectopic tachycardia was excluded — “JET could be excluded for the following reasons. First, the Purkinje potential at the first ablation site was earlier than at the His bundle during tachycardia. Second, in this case, the QRS morphology gradually changed to an RBBB pattern, and the His bundle potential that preceded the QRS complex disappeared after RF energy application … Third, RF energy application to a site remote from the His bundle successfully eliminated the tachycardia.”  
3. Reentrant fascicular VT was unlikely because of verapamil refractoriness — “Unlike reentrant fascicular VT, it is usually not responsive to verapamil; however, it is responsive to lidocaine and β-blocker treatment.”  
4. Nonreentrant focal Purkinje VT was diagnosed based on its features — “the tachycardia initiated and terminated incessantly and spontaneously, had an irregular cycle length, was refractory to verapamil, and was not entrained.”
